threats.title: Order records intercepted between kiosk and sync service
threats.description: Customer order records — name, delivery address, and order contents — travel from the kiosks over the store network to the sync service. Nothing in the note describes protection of that traffic.
preconditions: an attacker can observe store-network traffic
threats.impact: Customer names, delivery addresses, and order contents are disclosed.

threats.title: Forged order records submitted to the sync service
threats.description: The note says the kiosks call the service over the store network and nothing about how callers are identified. A device on that network that can reach the service could submit records the fulfillment system would then act on.
preconditions: the service accepts submissions without establishing the caller
attack_path: reach the service from the store network
threats.impact: The fulfillment system acts on orders no customer placed.

threats.title: Stored order records accumulate and are exposed
threats.description: The service stores order records for fulfillment to read; nothing describes how long they are kept or how the store is protected. The longer records accumulate, the more a later compromise discloses.
preconditions: records are retained without a bound
an attacker reaches the stored records
attack_path: compromise the service or its virtual machine
threats.impact: The accumulated history of customer orders is disclosed.
